                  <ns0:head>CHAP. XXXVI.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p n="1">1. NOw <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Kin. 18. 13. 2 Chr. 32. 1.</ns0:note> it came to pass in the fourteenth year of king <ns0:hi>Hezekiah, that Sennacherib</ns0:hi> king of <ns0:hi>Assyria</ns0:hi> came up against all the defenced cities of <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> and took them.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2. And the king of <ns0:hi>Assyria</ns0:hi> sent <ns0:hi>Rabshakeh,</ns0:hi> from <ns0:hi>Lachish</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> unto king <ns0:hi>Hezekiah,</ns0:hi> with a great army; and he stood by the conduit of the upper pool, in the high way of the ful<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lers field.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3. Then came forth unto him <ns0:hi>Eliakim Hil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />kiahs</ns0:hi> son, which <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> over the house, and <ns0:hi>Sheb<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />na</ns0:hi> the <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> secreta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> scribe, and <ns0:hi>Ioah Asaphs</ns0:hi> son the recor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4. And <ns0:hi>Rabshakeh</ns0:hi> said unto them, say ye now to <ns0:hi>Hezekiah,</ns0:hi> Thus saith the great king, the king of <ns0:hi>Assyria,</ns0:hi> What confidence <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> this wherein thou trustest?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5. I say, <ns0:hi>saist thou</ns0:hi> (but <ns0:hi>they are but</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> a word of lips.</ns0:note> vain words) <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, but <ns0:hi>coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sel and strength</ns0:hi> are <ns0:hi>for the war.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>I have</ns0:hi> counsel and strength for war: now on whom dost thou trust, that thou rebel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lest against me?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6. Lo, thou trustest in the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ezek. 29. 6, 7.</ns0:note> staff of this broken reed, on <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> whereon if a man lean, it will go into his hand and pierce it; so <ns0:hi>is Pharaoh</ns0:hi> king of <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> to all that trust in him.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7. But if thou say to me, We trust in the LORD our God: <ns0:hi>is it</ns0:hi> not he, whose high pla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces, and whose altars <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi> hath taken a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />way, and said to <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> and to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> Ye shall worship before this altar?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8. Now therefore give <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> hostages.</ns0:note> pledges, I pray thee, to my master the king of <ns0:hi>Assyria,</ns0:hi> and I will give thee two thousand horses, if thou be able on thy part to set riders upon them.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9. How then wilt thou turn away the face of one captain of the least of my masters servants, and put thy trust on <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> for chariots and for horsemen?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10. And am I now come up without the LORD against this land to destroy it? the LORD said unto me, Go up against this land, and destroy it.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11. Then said <ns0:hi>Eliakim,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Shebna,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ioah</ns0:hi> unto <ns0:hi>Rabshakeh,</ns0:hi> Speak, I pray thee, unto thy servants in the <ns0:hi>Syrian</ns0:hi> language, for we under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand <ns0:hi>it:</ns0:hi> and speak not to us in the Jews lan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />guage, in the ears of the people that <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> on the wall.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12. But <ns0:hi>Rabshakeh</ns0:hi> said, Hath my master sent me to thy master and to thee, to speak these words? <ns0:hi>hath</ns0:hi> he not <ns0:hi>sent me</ns0:hi> to the men that sit upon the wall, that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own piss with you?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13. Then <ns0:hi>Rabshakeh</ns0:hi> stood, and cried with a loud voice in the Jews language, and said, Hear ye the words of the great king, the king of <ns0:hi>Assyria.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14. Thus saith the king, Let not <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi> deceive you, for he shall not be able to deli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver you.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15. Neither let <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi> make you trust in the LORD, saying, The LORD will surely de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />liver us, this city shall not be delivered into the hand of the king of <ns0:hi>Assyria.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 Hearken not to <ns0:hi>Hezekiah,</ns0:hi> for thus saith the king of <ns0:hi>Assyria,</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> seek my favour by a pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sent.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> make with me a bles<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing.</ns0:note> Make an agreement with me by a present, and come out to me, and eat ye every one of his vine, and every one of his fig-tree, and drink ye every one the waters of his own cistern.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17. Untill I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of corn and wine, a land of bread and vineyards.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18. <ns0:hi>Beware</ns0:hi> lest <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi> perswade you, say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, the LORD will deliver us. Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of <ns0:hi>Assyria?</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19. Where <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> the gods of <ns0:hi>Hamath,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Arphad?</ns0:hi> where <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> the gods of <ns0:hi>Sepharvaim?</ns0:hi> and have they delivered <ns0:hi>Samaria</ns0:hi> out of my hand?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20. Who <ns0:hi>are they</ns0:hi> amongst all the gods of these lands, that have delivered their land out of my hand, that the LORD should deliver <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> out of my hand?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21. But they held their peace, and answered him not a word, for the kings commandment was, saying, Answer him not.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="22">22. Then came <ns0:hi>Eliakim</ns0:hi> the son of <ns0:hi>Hilkiah,</ns0:hi> that <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> over the houshold, and <ns0:hi>Shebna</ns0:hi> the scribe, and <ns0:hi>Ioah</ns0:hi> the son of<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Asaph</ns0:hi> the recorder, to <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi> with <ns0:hi>their</ns0:hi> cloths rent, and told him the words of <ns0:hi>Rabshakeh.</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:note place="bottom">The History related here, and in the Three following Chap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ters, is, for the substance of it, and almost wholly, in the same words contained, 2 <ns0:hi>Kings, chap.</ns0:hi> 18. & 19. & 20. It is fitly inserted here, to explain and confirm some of the foregoing Predictions. It may seem to have been first Written by this Prophet<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and from him to have been taken into the Book of <ns0:hi>Kings,</ns0:hi> to compleat that History.</ns0:note>
                  </ns0:p>
               </ns0:div>
